As the race progresses, the distance gap grows, indicating a stable performance advantage. The crew effort resilience reflects the system's ability to maintain high-intensity output despite fatigue. These primitives form a coherent dynamical system where each variable influences the others. The transition from competitive parity to decisive lead occurs when the gap surpasses a critical threshold, rendering reversal improbable. This mirrors a phase transition in thermodynamic systems, where small perturbations compound into macroscopic outcomes. The failure modes include loss of synchronization, mechanical inefficiency, or physiological collapse, all of which manifest as deviations from expected trajectories.
